title: SecOps-NG Playbook Mappings Overlay
description: Per-playbook outbound view of the content model: pins OSCAL controls, MITRE D3FEND defensive techniques, OCSF event classes, and the EU regulatory clauses (NIS2, DORA, CRA) this playbook helps operationalise. One file lives at content/playbooks/<slug>/mappings.yaml. Each top-level key holds an array of structural pointers; siblings in content/mappings/<regime>/ hold the inbound regulator-side view so the graph is closed in both directions. Placeholder IDs marked with `todo: true` are permitted while a playbook is still in SKELETON / CORE / EXTEND build-out.

playbook.description: Long-form URN of the playbook this overlay belongs to. Must match the playbook artifact's x_secops_ng.stable_id.

oscal.description: OSCAL control pointers exercised by this playbook. Each entry pins a control catalog (typically NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5) and a control_id. SKELETON entries may use placeholder control IDs with todo: true.

d3fend.description: MITRE D3FEND defensive technique tags for individual playbook steps. Lets a reviewer see the countermeasure shape without reading runtime code. SKELETON entries may use placeholder d3fend_id with todo: true.

ocsf.description: OCSF event classes consumed or emitted by this playbook. SKELETON entries may use placeholder class_uid with todo: true.

nis2.description: NIS2 cross-references this playbook helps operationalise. Each entry pins a mapping id from content/mappings/nis2/*.yaml so the graph is closed in both directions. SKELETON entries may use todo: true and a placeholder mapping_id while the inbound side is being populated.

dora.description: DORA cross-references this playbook helps operationalise. Each entry pins a mapping id from content/mappings/dora/*.yaml so the graph is closed in both directions. SKELETON entries may use todo: true and a placeholder mapping_id while the inbound side is being populated.

cra.description: CRA (Cyber Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) cross-references this playbook helps operationalise. Each entry pins a mapping id from content/mappings/cra/*.yaml so the graph is closed in both directions. SKELETON entries may use todo: true and a placeholder mapping_id while the inbound side is being populated.

gdpr.description: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) cross-references this playbook helps operationalise. Each entry pins a mapping id from content/mappings/gdpr/*.yaml so the graph is closed in both directions. Optional at the playbook level: absence means the playbook has no direct GDPR touchpoint. SKELETON entries may use todo: true and a placeholder mapping_id while the inbound side is being populated.

eu_ai_act.description: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) cross-references this playbook helps operationalise. Each entry pins a mapping id from content/mappings/eu_ai_act/*.yaml so the graph is closed in both directions. Optional at the playbook level: absence means the playbook has no direct EU AI Act touchpoint. SKELETON entries may use todo: true and a placeholder mapping_id while the inbound side is being populated.

soc2.description: SOC 2 (AICPA Trust Services Criteria) cross-references this playbook helps operationalise. Each entry pins a mapping id from content/mappings/soc2/*.yaml so the graph is closed in both directions. Optional at the playbook level: absence means the playbook has no direct SOC 2 touchpoint. Note that SOC 2 is not an EU statutory instrument — per docs/cookbook/soc2_crosswalk.md the EU mappings remain the authoritative pointer for the statutory surface, and a soc2 block never replaces one.

todo_flag.description: Marks the entry as a SKELETON placeholder. Sibling CORE / EXTEND cards replace placeholder fields with real IDs and clear this flag.

control_ref.description: Optional reference to the SecOps-NG control that discharges this catalog control, as `control.<slug>@v<semver>`. When present it MUST resolve to a committed file under `content/controls/` — this field is a reference, not a label. Omit it where no SecOps-NG control models the discipline: the catalog anchor is already carried by `oscal_catalog` + `control_id` + `title`, and a URN restating the catalog title adds nothing. Replaces the former `id`, which was required, had no machine consumer, and was used as a free label in 116 of 182 entries — see the arch decision recorded in issue #853.

step.description: Optional CACAO step/action UUID this technique applies to.

d3fend_id.description: MITRE D3FEND technique identifier, e.g. 'D3-OSM'. SKELETON placeholder: 'D3-TODO'.

id.description: Reference to the OCSF telemetry class this playbook consumes or emits, as `telemetry.ocsf.<class>@v<semver>`. It MUST resolve to a committed artifact under `content/telemetry/` — this is a reference, not a label, and the `ocsf` segment is part of the name. The bare `telemetry.<class>@v1` spelling is wrong: 63 of 91 entries used it until #873 normalised them, and it escaped into a metric by being copied out of an overlay. Enforced by tools/lint_playbook_telemetry_refs.py. SKELETON placeholders use `telemetry.todo_<slug>@v0`.

direction.description: Whether this playbook consumes or emits the class.

mapping_id.description: Mapping id from content/mappings/nis2/*.yaml that this playbook backlinks to.

article.description: Article reference shorthand, e.g. '21(2)(d)'. Informational; the authoritative citation lives on the inbound mapping entry.

mapping_id.description: Mapping id from content/mappings/dora/*.yaml that this playbook backlinks to.

article.description: Article reference shorthand, e.g. '19(2)'. Informational; the authoritative citation lives on the inbound mapping entry.

mapping_id.description: Mapping id from content/mappings/cra/*.yaml that this playbook backlinks to.

article.description: Article / annex reference shorthand, e.g. 'Annex I §1(b)' or '13(6)'. Informational; the authoritative citation lives on the inbound mapping entry.
